final_answer:
The computational security status of the AES-256 encryption standard against brute-force attacks is considered to be high, but not completely unbreakable. While there have been some theoretical attacks published that can recover the key of a reduced-round version of AES-256, these attacks are not practical against the full 256-bit key. Quantum attacks are also not considered a significant threat to AES-256 due to its quantum resistance being similar to AES-128. However, it's important to note that the security of AES-256 may be affected by side-channel attacks or other vulnerabilities in the implementation.
